author: mindmap-write-lane-c
readerQuestion: How much will a bridge loan cost me until my old home sells? [PAA 2/6 adjacent (does a bridge loan cost more; how do you calculate loan to cost), 4/6 off-topic: construction loan payment, 20% down payment, mortgage qualification; ac 3/16 question completions incl. how much bridge loan can i get, how much bridge loan cost]

presentation.placement: New real-estate spoke; calculator is section 1
presentation.reason: The cost depends on loan size, rate, fees and how many months the old home takes to sell, which only the reader knows.
readerInputs: Expected sale price of the old home
Months until the old home sells

interaction.reason: Months-to-sell is the main swing factor and changes the answer; a fixed example hides it.

animation.reason: Month count is a single number; a cost-by-month table shows the sensitivity without animation.

caseDecisions: Retrieved with the exact approved reader question. 8 candidates, none about 401(k) plan loans, short-term real estate loans or ModernWallet readers: they are other Layer3Labs properties, client engagements and a gaming testimonial. ModernWallet's _experience.md has no named-client specifics. Rejected all; no client claim on the page.
exclusions: No TESTED label and no reviewed-by claim: financial service, _experience.md section G excludes it and no product test exists. Internal-modeling wording only.
decisionGap: Readers can find what a bridge loan is, but not what their own timeline costs: fees plus months of interest, on top of carrying two homes, taken out of the old home's proceeds. Sampled the 2026-11-14 research pack and DataForSEO read; no site-wide uniqueness claimed.
finding: In our internal modeling of one example sale (old home sells for $400,000, old mortgage payoff $200,000, bridge loan $100,000 at 10% APR with a 2% fee, 6 months, 6% selling costs), bridge interest is $5,000, fees are $2,000, bridge cost is $7,000, selling costs are $24,000 and net proceeds are $69,000. The same loan costs $4,500 at 3 months, $9,500 at 9 months and $12,000 at 12 months, leaving $71,500, $66,500 and $64,000. With a $2,500 new mortgage payment and $1,800 of old-home carrying costs, the overlap outlay is $4,300 a month, $25,800 over 6 months. Against an example alternative costing $1,500 a month with no up-front fee, the bridge costs less once the old home takes more than 3.0 months to sell. A $300,000 payoff makes net proceeds negative $31,000.
conditions: Reader-entered terms only; every rate, fee and limit in the example is an illustrative input, not a lender quote or market figure. Interest is simple and repaid from the sale proceeds; carrying costs are entered by the reader (old mortgage payment, taxes, insurance, utilities).
whatWouldChange: A lender quote with different fees or rate, a sale that takes longer or shorter, interest paid monthly instead of at payoff, prepayment terms, closing costs on the new home, or taxes on the sale.
method: Deterministic: interest = loan x APR/12 x months; fees = loan x origination% + other fees; bridge cost = fees + interest; net proceeds = sale - payoff - bridge loan - bridge cost - selling costs; overlap outlay = new mortgage payment + old home carrying costs; break-even months = fees/(alternative monthly - bridge monthly interest). Python replica of src/lib/bridge-loan.ts.
limitations: No lender rates, fees, terms or loan-to-value limits; net proceeds ignore closing costs on the new home and taxes; the break-even compares against one entered alternative with no up-front fee.
counterexample: With a payoff of $300,000 instead of $200,000 the same sale leaves negative $31,000, and with no origination fee the cost falls from $7,000 to $5,000, so fees are not the only lever; if the alternative costs no more per month than the bridge interest of $833.33, the bridge never costs less.

provenance.publicMethod: settlement convention and formulas stated next to the tool and in the worked example
provenance.placement: introText worked example plus What a Bridge Loan Costs Month by Month

medium: interactive tool: sale price, payoff, loan, rate, fees and months to sell change the cost and the net proceeds
